synopsis: The booklet treats GAO and AACE guides as recognized yardsticks for auditable budgets and deadline claims, and recommends GAO cost and schedule checklists as structures for the validation plan [f16431, f16443, f9983]. GAO's Schedule Assessment Guide (GAO-16-89G, December 2015) provides ten best-practice areas, including schedule-risk analysis; the booklet calls for an integrated schedule with reference classes, range assumptions, an S-curve, a critical path, buffers and long-lead items [f9627, f16433, f16438]. The recommended schedule and basis-of-estimate section is 1–3 pages, with detailed schedules, reference-class data and elicitation records in Appendix F [f10172, f10187]. GAO's Cost Estimating and Assessment Guide (GAO-20-195G, March 2020) is the recommended companion template for capability costs, while AACE 57R-09 describes integrated cost and schedule risk analysis using risk drivers and Monte Carlo simulation of a critical-path model [f16434, f10374, f16436]. Cost estimation was omitted from the research questions; the booklet nevertheless recommends bottom-up estimates after pilots and vendor quotations for tool budgets because public prices are almost entirely absent [f16439, f11084, f16441]. GAO audits spanning 2005–2026 associate immature technology and optimistic commitment timelines with failure, and knowledge-based practices with better outcomes, but these findings are correlational rather than causal [f10288, f10289].
